subject: Discovery recap: tool/function-calling & structured output requirements
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Discovery recap: tool/function-calling & structured output requirements

Alex — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps so we all have the same picture. High-level notes: 

Pain points
- Current system: ad-hoc prompt wrappers calling third-party LLM APIs; inconsistent output leading to manual post-processing.
- Need deterministic, schema-compliant responses for downstream automation (order ingestion, SLA routing).
- Latency spikes on peak loads; want predictable 95th pct latency under 300ms for interactive flows.

Current stack
- Backend: AWS Fargate + Lambda for orchestration.
- LLM: experimenting with public API + occasional private model hosting.
- Observability: internal logs + Datadog.

Success criteria for a POC
1) Accuracy: >= 95% JSON schema validation pass rate on target prompts (1000 sample prompts).
2) Determinism: Stable field ordering and types across retries; minimal variability in non-volatile fields.
3) Latency: 95th pct < 300ms for single-turn tool calls at target concurrency (10 rps).
4) Cost: token/unit cost reduction vs current setup by >= 20% (estimated).

Tool / function-calling requirements we discussed
- Primary workflow: user query -> agent decides to call external tool (inventory lookup, pricing API) -> LLM returns structured JSON payload following a strict schema -> orchestration layer executes tool and returns final user-facing message.
- JSON schema must be strict: required fields, types (string/number/enum), and explicit error code fields. We should reject payloads that fail validation rather than try to patch them downstream.
- Deterministic formatting: we recommend canonical field ordering + explicit null vs absent semantics.
- Example behaviours: if model cannot confidently populate a required field, return {"field": null, "reason": "low_confidence"} rather than freeform text.

Deliverables I will share after this email
- Draft JSON schema for the tool-calling payload (attached: acme_tool_calling_schema_v1.json).
- Proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for a 6-week POC (attached PDF).
- Link to a short technical deep-dive (we can schedule next week) if your infra team wants to go deeper.

Next steps
1) I’ll send the schema and MAP (attached).
2) Can we schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineers next Tue or Wed?
3) Alex — could you confirm the sample prompt set (we discussed ~1k examples) and share an initial list by end of week?

Thanks again — pleased with how aligned this was.

—
Jordan Blake

Jordan — really helpful recap, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed pain points: we want to eliminate manual parsing work and reduce failed automations that require human intervention.
- Sample prompt set: we can deliver ~1k prompts, mixing edge cases and high-frequency requests; target delivery by Friday EOD.
- Security: we need SOC2 evidence and details on data retention for the POC. Can your CSM/Trust team provide a short summary?
- SSO/SCIM: must work with Okta (SCIM + SAML).

On deterministic JSON: yes — we must have strict validation. We prefer that any schema failure surface as a structured error object so our orchestration can route to a retry or manual review.
